hero.lede: The code-first headless CMS that feels at home in your Angular application. Model in TypeScript, give editors a real Angular admin, and keep the site UI yours.

story.title: Everything between your schema and your client’s editor.
story.lede: Five steps from a TypeScript file to a site your client runs. Each one is part of the published 1.0 release.

schema.label: Schema
schema.title: Model the content once, in code.
schema.body: A collection is plain TypeScript in your repository: fields, drafts, locales and access rules, reviewed like any other change.

runtime.label: Runtime
runtime.title: One pipeline for every read and write.
runtime.body: Server code calls the Local API with no HTTP hop; browsers use REST. Both run the same access, hooks, drafts and validation.

angular.label: Angular
angular.title: Your components read typed signals.
angular.body: The Angular client turns a collection into a signal resource typed from your schema, rendered on the server with Analog and hydrated.

admin.label: Admin
admin.title: Your client gets a real editor.
admin.body: The reusable Angular admin mounts under your own routes: content, drafts, media, users and both languages, with nothing to hand-build.

deploy.label: Deploy
deploy.title: Ship it where it fits.
deploy.body: Cloudflare Pages with D1 and R2, or any Node host with libSQL and S3-compatible storage. Both profiles are certified from packed artifacts.

purpose.core: Schema DSL, validation, collection and global definitions
purpose.db: Database contract, InMemory and libSQL adapters, schema sync
purpose.auth: Users collection auth, sessions, API keys
purpose.s3: S3-compatible StorageAdapter for portable durable file storage
purpose.runtime: Local API, access, hooks, drafts, HTTP handlers
purpose.cloudflare: D1 database and R2 storage adapters
purpose.angular: Typed client, signal resources, auth session and guard
purpose.admin: Embeddable Angular admin: content, users, sign-in
purpose.agent: Read-only MCP server and official skills for coding agents

packages.adapters: Databases: InMemory, libSQL and Cloudflare D1. Storage: InMemory, Cloudflare R2 and an S3-compatible service (Garage is the one certified in CI; AWS S3, Backblaze B2 and Wasabi are configurable, not certified). Two durable profiles are certified: Cloudflare (D1 + R2) and portable (libSQL + S3).

roadmap.title: A shipped foundation. A clear next direction.
roadmap.lede: ForgeCMS 1.0.0 is shipped. The V2 roadmap focuses on stronger editorial workflows, developer experience, and production operations.

demo.editorLede: Publish something and watch it move.

site.title: Look at the clinic site first
site.detail: Every word, price, image and opening hour on it is content, not code. The home page itself is a list of blocks an editor arranged.

browse.title: Sign in and browse the content
browse.detail: Open Treatments, Team and Journal. Each is a collection with its own fields, drafts and relations. The hosted demo keeps these read-only so it stays intact for everyone.

locales.title: Switch the site between EN and ES
locales.detail: The "From the clinic" notice at the top is localized content. Open Content, then Notices, edit it in one locale, switch the locale and edit the other, then publish: each language keeps its own text and the public site updates. Notices are the part of the hosted demo you can edit.

booking.title: Send yourself a booking
booking.detail: Fill in the booking form on the public site, then open Bookings in the CMS. It arrives as pending, and only staff can see it.

limits.title: See what the hosted demo limits
limits.detail: The hosted demo limits deletes, new documents, uploads and settings changes so the example stays available. Your own ForgeCMS project has none of these demo limits. Clone the demo to try uploads and every edit.

traffic.title: Check the site traffic (experimental)
traffic.detail: The overview and Analytics pages show real visits from Cloudflare Analytics Engine when it is configured, or say plainly that it is not. There are never placeholder numbers.

demo.developerTitle: Inspect it as an Angular developer
demo.developerLede: Follow the model into the runtime and UI.

model.title: The content model is one TypeScript file
model.detail: apps/demo-aesthetics/src/server/api/collections.ts — twelve collections with drafts, hooks, row-level access rules, composite fields and one localized collection. That file is the whole schema.

localApi.title: The server talks to the CMS with no HTTP hop
localApi.detail: src/server/routes/api/site/home.get.ts composes five collections into one payload through the Local API (runtime.find/create), with access control and draft rules applied.

localization.title: Localization uses the supported contract
localization.detail: The notices collection localizes top-level text and textarea fields only. The public read passes a locale and runs as an anonymous visitor, so drafts never leak in either language.

writes.title: Public writes are decided by the collection, not the route
writes.detail: The booking form posts as nobody. The bookings collection allows it via access.create, and a hook forces status back to pending so a crafted request cannot self-confirm.

admin.title: The admin is a package, not app code
admin.detail: @forge-cms/admin ships the layout, sign-in session, collection list, document editor and staff accounts. The app mounts its routes, sets its own navigation and keeps only clinic-specific pages.

dogfood.title: Analytics and Agent Kit are dogfooded
dogfood.detail: Analytics (experimental) is wired with the documented recipe. The Agent Kit is development tooling: a test points its read-only MCP at this project and checks it is detected. It is not part of the demo runtime.

tests.title: Run the tests to see the rules
tests.detail: pnpm test:demo drives the content model through the typed Local API: who can read a booking, what a draft is invisible to, what a hook rewrites, how a notice resolves per locale.

demo.accountsTitle: Use the same CMS the clinic uses.
demo.accountsBody: Try the real admin. Everyone shares the database, so the hosted demo limits destructive and storage-heavy actions — you can edit and publish the localized notices and send a booking — to keep the example available for the next visitor. Your own ForgeCMS project does not have these shared-demo limits.
demo.sourceTitle: The source is part of the demo.
demo.sourceBody: The content model, Local API composition and app-side findings are public. The rough edges are documented alongside the working paths.

privacy.title: Website audience measurement
privacy.useBody: The ForgeCMS website offers optional, basic pageview statistics through a self-hosted Umami service at {#code}{$host}{/code}. The tracker is not loaded unless you choose “Allow analytics”. We use the statistics to understand visits to public website pages.
privacy.infoBody: When enabled, this site sends the public website identifier and the current public page path. Query strings, fragments, page titles, referrers and click events are excluded. The request also necessarily exposes network headers such as your IP address and browser User-Agent to the service. Umami's published documentation says it uses the IP address for approximate location without storing it, and calculates rotating session hashes from values including the User-Agent. The exact deployed Umami version and server configuration have not yet been independently verified.
privacy.storageBody: Umami's tracker documentation says it does not use cookies. This website stores your analytics choice in browser local storage so it can remember it; no analytics data is stored in that preference.
privacy.choiceBody: The tracker stays off until you explicitly opt in; consent is the basis used for this optional measurement. You can change your choice here. The AEPD's audience-measurement exemption has not been established for this service because its processing terms, server configuration and retention have not been confirmed. The server-side retention period is currently unknown, so analytics remains consent-gated.
privacy.rightsBody: The project has not published a controller identity or privacy contact address. Those owner-provided details, together with the service's data-processing and deletion arrangements, must be confirmed before this notice can be complete. Once identified, contact the controller to exercise applicable data-protection rights, including access, erasure, restriction and objection. You may also contact the Spanish Data Protection Agency (AEPD).
privacy.references: References: {#tracker}Umami tracker configuration{/tracker}, {#metrics}Umami metric definitions{/metrics}, and {#aepd}AEPD audience-measurement guidance{/aepd}.

consent.title: Optional audience analytics
consent.body: Umami helps us understand which public pages are useful. It stays off unless you allow it. {#link}Read the privacy notice{/link}.
